about: Today's Rust layout of the syntax tree's records: what nodes.schema.json (the field schema) does not say
and scripts/generate_nodes.py needs to render nodes.rs, for_each_child.rs, relocate.rs and
observable_fields.rs. Every entry carries a one-line reason ('why').

record.why: Node = 24 B header + 24 B NodeData (1 B tag, payload at offset 4); a payload over 20 B or with 8-byte alignment is boxed

boxed.why: a JSDocComment (est. 40 B) or a text (24 B) does not fit the 20 B inline payload
a literal's text (24 B, 8-byte aligned) does not fit the 20 B inline payload
six or more child slots (24 B or more) do not fit the 20 B inline payload
boxed with the text literals by f6fde16e6; the payload is zero-sized, so the Box never allocates

JsString.why: string literal values hold arbitrary UTF-16 (lone surrogates); numeric, raw and identifier texts stay UTF-8

EscapedName.why: an identifier's escaped text is the interned name the binder keys its tables by, at the size of an id

rustOptional.JSDocNamepathType.type: the JSDoc parser creates JSDocNamepathType(undefined) while recovering, though the d.ts says required

JSDocParameterTag.why: tsc visits name before typeExpression only when isNameFirst

JSDocPropertyTag.why: tsc visits name before typeExpression only when isNameFirst

JSDocTypedefTag.why: tsc visits typeExpression before fullName only when it is a JSDocTypeExpression

headerObservables.name: isUnterminated
headerObservables.why: kept in the header's literal_flags, not in the payload

headerObservables.name: hasExtendedUnicodeEscape
headerObservables.why: kept in the header's literal_flags, not in the payload

equalitySkips.ModuleDeclaration.attributes: 2517f726b added the field by hand but not to node_data_structurally_equal; kept as is (a fix candidate)

ModuleDeclaration.attributes: TypeScript 7.1's import attributes type of an ambient module
